subject: Launch window: options for temporary headroom, overrun conversion, and package adjustments
messages:
From: Claire Dalton <claire@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Need short-window headroom + alternative to emergency overrun charges

Marcus —

We’re three days out from BrightCart’s feature-driven marketing push and our traffic forecast just jumped up ~3.2x for the first 48 hours. Our engineering team asked whether we can get temporary runway above our committed quota and whether there’s a better way to handle the expected overrun than paying the listed overage rate.

Quick background: we’re on the Standard commit (200M tokens / month) and expect to hit ~640M tokens total during the first two days of the campaign. Procurement will need an email trail for approvals; ideally we’d avoid a surprise invoice. Can Redwood offer either: (A) a temporary headroom allotment billed as a one-time uplift at a discounted overrun rate, or (B) convert the expected incremental usage into a short-term higher commit for Jan with a pro-rata true-up and a modest launch discount?

I attached the projected usage export and the current MSA for reference. We need a decision by EOD tomorrow PST.

—Claire
Claire Dalton
Head of Growth, BrightCart
claire@brightcart.com

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dalton <claire@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Need short-window headroom + alternative to emergency overrun charges

Thanks Claire — timely ask and appreciate the attachment. High level options we can execute quickly: 

1) Temporary Headroom Credit (fastest): we provision an ephemeral headroom pool for 72 hours equal to the delta (440M tokens). We can offer a 35% discount off-list overage rate for that pool. Invoice will show a single line item; no contract amendment needed.

2) Short-term Commit Conversion (procurement-friendly): we convert 440M tokens into a one-month elevated commit (addendum) with a pro-rata true-up and a 20% launch discount on the uplift. This requires a signed addendum (DocuSign) and PO routing — we can turn it around in <24 hours if procurement is ready.

3) Hybrid: give 200M headroom credit (fast), and convert the remaining 240M into the short-term commit (requires addendum).

Which path is preferable depends on procurement tolerance for signing an addendum vs. speed. I’ve CC’d Monica (customer success) to help with rollout and billing, and pulled Ben (our pricing lead) into the thread internally to confirm margin impact. I’ll follow up with proposed numbers and the DocuSign link if you want option 2.

Attaching a short spreadsheet with the math.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: BrightCart_usage_Jul2027.csv (usage snapshot)

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Need short-window headroom + alternative to emergency overrun charges

Internal — see BrightCart ask below. They want a clean path procurement will sign quickly but also prefer a minimal surprise invoice. Proposed pricing impact: if we do Temporary Headroom Credit at -35% it’s roughly $9.6k gross for the delta; Commit Conversion at -20% reduces price but requires PO + addendum. Can legal/finance fast-track a one-month addendum? Also want to check whether we can make the DocuSign addendum auto-populate the exact pro-rate and note the launch window.

Ben — thoughts on margin and whether we should offer a minor promotional credit for a longer-term commit conversion? Could be a good land-and-expand moment.

Monica — if we do option 1, can CS coordinate throttling windows and a cleanup plan post-launch? They want to avoid token double-counting and ensure KV cache behavior isn’t penalized.

—Marcus

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Need short-window headroom + alternative to emergency overrun charges

All — margin check: option 1 (ephemeral headroom @ -35%) is acceptable for a one-off, but given they are enterprise-pace and likely to expand we should push for option 2 and give a modest sweetener: 15% additional credit if they convert the Jan uplift into a 3-month committed tier within 30 days. That gives us runway to recover capacity and encourages stickiness.

Naomi — can legal prep a templated one-month addendum that 1) lists the boosted token commit for Jan only, 2) pro-rates billing, 3) includes a discrete launch window clause, and 4) calls out that any persistent baseline increase reverts to negotiated commit after the month? We should avoid permanent SLA changes.

If procurement needs an immediate invoice-friendly path, we send the Headroom Credit now and open the addendum lane.

—Ben
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dalton <claire@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jan 2028 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Need short-window headroom + alternative to emergency overrun charges — proposed path and next steps

Claire — thanks for the quick turn. Based on internal alignment here’s a recommended two-step path that balances speed and procurement governance: 

• Step A (Immediate, <2 hours): we provision a 72-hour temporary headroom pool sized to the delta (440M tokens) and apply a 35% off-list overrun discount. This avoids surprise charges and gives your engineering team headroom for the launch. You will get a single, transparent line item.

• Step B (90-minute procurement lane): simultaneously we’ll issue a one-month addendum converting 440M tokens into a Jan elevated commit at 20% off uplift price. The addendum is prefilled for you — sign via DocuSign if procurement prefers the commit. If BrightCart signs within 30 days and subsequently converts the uplift into a 3-month commit, we’ll apply the additional 15% conversion credit on the uplift portion.

Action items: 
1) Please confirm whether you want us to 1) only provision Step A (headroom) or 2) provision headroom and open the DocuSign addendum for procurement to sign (we recommend both).
2) If you want the addendum, loop in your PO owner and CC procurement@brightcart.com; we’ll send the DocuSign link immediately.

I attached the proposed addendum (pdf) and the usage extract you sent. If you confirm I’ll 1) kick the headroom and 2) route the DocuSign link.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
Attachment: BrightCart_Proposed_Addendum_v1.pdf
Links: https://www.docusign.com/BR-5491-addendum
